rules.statement: The authorization cookie is read as a token only when cosec.pipeline.allow-cookie-token is on, and it is off by default: a browser sends a cookie on its own, on a cross-site request too, so a host that turns it on defends against CSRF itself. rules.statement: A path with an empty segment before its end (`//`, also as removing a path parameter leaves it), an encoded separator (`%2F`, in either case) or a backslash (`\`, or `%5C` in either case) is answered 400 before authentication: a pattern reads them as segments of their own or as part of one, so a DENY would not match what a backend that merges slashes, decodes separators or reads a backslash as a separator serves. A trailing `/` is read as written, and a double-encoded separator (`%252F`, `%255C`) decodes to text.

rules.statement: A check by host code (`AuthorizationChecker`) never permits what enforcement would refuse to decide: an `http` path is normalized as a request's path is, one enforcement answers 400 for is a deny, and any other resource is held to a request path's length bounds. An `http` action is read as a request's method is (`PIP-18`): a verb with a lower-case letter is a deny, and `http:HEAD` is decided as `http:GET`. The test kit (`PolicyTestKit`) reads a scenario's action and resource the same way, so it decides what the pipeline decides for that request, and what enforcement answers 400 for is its `InvalidRequest` (round 2 review of host and tools, M2).

rules.statement: A client address the host reported that is not an address (`unknown`, an obfuscated identifier) is unavailable, never absent: a statement that reads `environment.ip` errs as on a missing external attribute (a DENY is Indeterminate unless `onMissing: nomatch`), and the blacklist cannot be read for it. A trusted `X-Forwarded-For` entry or a peer written with a port, brackets or a zone is read as its address, and several `X-Forwarded-For` lines are one list, in order.

A method holding an ASCII lower-case letter is 400 `invalid-request`, before authentication. HEAD is decided as GET: a route map's HEAD route wins, without one HEAD takes GET's route, and unmapped it is `http:GET`; `http:HEAD` matches nothing unless a route map maps it.

On both web stacks the adapter runs after Spring Boot's filters that rewrite the request (the hidden-method filter), and before everything that acts on it, so CoSec authorizes the request that is executed.

rules.statement: A check by host code (`AuthorizationChecker`, in every form: the public one, and the control plane's in another app and as a recorded principal) is answered for a request in progress however long it runs, on the memberships and attributes it began with, also once its token has expired; once the adapter that bound the request has ended it, every check of it is an implicit deny (`Deny(null)`). The WebFlux and gateway adapters end a request when the chain's `Mono` terminates (after a streamed body's last element is written, on an error, or when the client goes away), before they pass its completion or error on, so a subscriber that sees the chain complete sees the request ended; the servlet filter when the dispatch returns, or, for an async request, when it completes, fails or times out. On the servlet containers the ERROR dispatch, which the filter does not take, finds the context and every check of it denied. A transport of the application's own that calls `Pipeline.evaluate` ends a request by closing its `Outcome` (`AutoCloseable`; nothing for a refused request; idempotent, and one end with an adapter's in either order); one that never closes it leaves the request in progress, and the test kit ends its contexts with `PipelineFixture.end` and `PermittedRequest.end`.

rules.statement: The request's `java.security.Principal` is CoSec's if and only if CoSec authenticated the request, on every web stack (WebFlux, the gateway, Spring MVC): a request CoSec authenticated carries CoSec's principal, the same object on all three (`exchange.getPrincipal()`; `getUserPrincipal()`, with `getRemoteUser()` its id), replacing whatever the container or a filter in front had set; a request CoSec treats as anonymous carries none of CoSec's, and what it already had (another layer's principal) is left as it was. On Spring MVC, where CoSec sets the principal `isUserInRole` answers false and `getAuthType()` null, since CoSec answers no container role and the wrapped request's belong to another principal; where it sets none both are the wrapped request's. The principal holds on an async request's ASYNC dispatch; the ERROR dispatch, which the filter does not take, carries none of CoSec's.

rules.statement: The kit's contexts are made by the pipeline: `PermittedRequest.forSubject` as the fixture's (an enforce-mode host's context, no credential, no forwarded identity), `withIdentity` by the identity gate from a `CoSec-Identity` header. A test binder (`CoSecTestBindings` of `cosec-testkit`, `me.ahoo.cosec.testkit.webflux` and `.webmvc`) binds only a context CoSec's pipeline made and refuses any other with an error naming what to use instead, so a test never runs as anonymous without saying so; its `filter` is the adapter itself and answers as the adapter does. A bound context whose request has ended is denied (`PIP-26`).

rules.statement: A path holding an encoded `;` (`%3B`) or an encoded control character (`%00` to `%1F`, `%7F`), in either case of the hex digits and anywhere in the path, path parameters included, is answered 400 before authentication, mapped route or not: CoSec reads them as text of a segment, but a backend that decodes before it strips path parameters, stops at NUL or drops what follows a control character serves another path than the one decided. A raw control character is answered the same way, whichever server hands the path over; a raw `;` is a path parameter. A double-encoded one (`%253B`, `%2500`) decodes to text, and a trailing dot or space is read as written.

rules.statement: A gateway forwards the request it decided: `PipelineGatewayFilter` removes the method-override headers `X-HTTP-Method-Override`, `X-HTTP-Method` and `X-Method-Override`, in any letter case, from every request it forwards, on every route, whether or not the route receives the identity, so a backend never runs a request as another method than the one the gateway decided (a DENY on `http:DELETE` is not stepped around by a `POST` that carries one of them). Not configurable. Every other header is forwarded as before. In-process hosts decide after Spring's hidden-method filter (`PIP-19`), and a service behind the gateway runs none (`STA-6`).

rules.source: Coordinator's brief for 8.0.0-beta.6, 2026-11-21 (the properties review, items 13 to 21 and 28; what can be computed is not configured)
rules.statement: Every stage's timeout is a share of the one deadline an operator states, `cosec.pipeline.timeout`, and the starter has no property for any of them: the authenticator 20 %, the membership provider (and the fill of the membership cache) 10 %, an attribute provider that sets no timeout of its own 6 %, the rate limiter 10 %, each read of CoSec's own revocation reader 30 % of the authentication's, a REQUIRED decision listener 20 % (`OBS-10`); each share is a named constant and never below a millisecond, and at the default deadline of 5 s each is the default its property had. A provider's or a reader's own bound (an `AttributeProvider` with its own timeout, an application's `RevocationReader`) stays its own. A key that once set one (`cosec.pipeline.authentication-timeout`, `cosec.authorization.membership.timeout`, `cosec.authorization.attributes.timeout`, `cosec.authorization.rate-limit.timeout`, `cosec.authentication.revocation.read-timeout`) fails startup as a key CoSec does not read, saying it is no longer a property and what replaced it, as do `cosec.authorization.snapshot.local-max-age` (3 revalidate intervals) and `cosec.authorization.membership.unknown-ttl` (a constant, 5 s). The starter says once at startup what each came to and from what.
